title: The Stolen Pearl (हिन्दी)
summary: A priceless pearl vanishes from Akbar's private chamber. Birbal uncovers which attendant took it by observing their nervous eyes. [HI]
full_text:
Emperor Akbar's private jewel master was arranging a tray of nine flawless Persian pearls in the Sheesh Mahal (Palace of Mirrors) when the Emperor summoned him to the balcony. Leaving the velvet tray on a marble table for barely three minutes, the jeweler returned to find the largest pearl—a gem the size of a pigeon's egg, worth a king's ransom—missing from its satin groove.

Only six palace chamberlains had been present in the hallway outside the room. All were trusted men from noble families. When interrogated, all six swore solemn oaths of innocence, tearing their robes in distress.

Akbar summoned Birbal: 'This pearl was an imperial treasure. Yet I cannot torture six noble youths without proof. How can we determine the guilty one?'

Birbal requested that all six chamberlains be brought into a quiet, darkened room lined with mirrors. He placed a bronze bowl filled with pure spring water upon a low table and addressed the men:

'In this holy water, I have dissolved an ancient herbal potion brought from Tibet. It has no smell, but when an innocent man looks into the water, his reflection appears calm and clear. However, when the man who holds the stolen pearl looks into the bowl, the water will instantly reveal a dark shadow over his brow, marking him for the executioner.'

Birbal instructed each man to walk alone to the table, look directly into the water, and return to his place.

Five of the chamberlains walked forward with steady, confident strides, leaned over the bowl, looked deeply into the water, and smiled in relief at their clear reflections.

However, the fourth chamberlain approached with trembling knees. His eyes darted nervously between the water and the ceiling. Terrified that the magic water would reveal his crime, he stepped to the table, squeezed his eyes tightly shut, held his breath, and backed away without looking into the water at all!

Birbal immediately grabbed the fourth chamberlain's wrist: 'Here is your thief, Your Majesty!'

'How can you know?' Akbar asked.

'Sire, the water is ordinary well water. Five innocent men looked into it without fear. But this man was so terrified of what the water might reveal that he closed his eyes tightly, refusing to look at his own reflection!'

The trembling youth fell to his knees, broke down in tears, and pulled the giant pearl from the hollow heel of his leather riding boot. Akbar praised Birbal's psychological genius, which extracted the truth without spilling a single drop of blood.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Stolen Pearl"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
